Bench: M.R. Shah, C.T. Ravikumar
 In The Supreme Court Of India

DELHI DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY ...APPELLANT(S)
 VERSUS  HIMANSHU GUPTA & ORS. .RESPONDENT(S)
 WITH  CIVIL APPEAL NO. OF 2023  (@ Special Leave Petition (C) No. of 2023)
 (@ Diary No. 7084/2023)
 O R D E R Delay condoned.
Leave granted.

Feeling aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order dated 06-07-2018 passed by the High Court of Delhi at New Delhi in Writ Petition (Civil) No. 1744/2016, by which the High Court has allowed the said writ petition and has declared that the acquisition with respect to the land in question is deemed to have lapsed under Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short the 2013 Act), the Delhi Development Authority as well as the Government of NCT of Delhi & Anr. have preferred the present appeals Reason:

entities.label: COURT

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
From the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court and even the counter affidavit filed by the contd..
- 2 - appellant(s) before the High Court, it was the specific case on behalf of the appellant(s) that the possession of the land in question being Khasra No. 676 was taken over on 31.12.2013.

However,
thereafter, solely on the ground that the compensation has not been paid/tendered, the High Court has allowed the said writ petition and has declared that the acquisition with respect to the land in Delhi Development Authority vs Himanshu Gupta on 8 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35203150/
1 question is deemed to have lapsed.

sentences.text: Ms. Uttara Babbar, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent(s) has vehemently submitted that even in the possession proceedings produced along with the SLP (Pgs. 60-62), there is no reference to Khasra No.676.

Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant(s) has placed on record the zerox copy of the hand written possession proceedings, in which there is a reference to Khasra No.676 and it is the case on behalf of the appellant(s) that in the typed copy produced before this Court, there is a typographical error.

It is also the case on behalf of the appellant(s) that even the High Court has also not disputed that the possession of Khasra No.676 was not taken over on 31.12.2013, as was the case on behalf of the appellant(s).
The view taken by the High Court is unsustainable in view of the decision of this Court in the case of Indore Development Authority vs. Manoharlal and Others, (2020) 8 SCC 129.

entities.text: Indore Development Authority vs. Manoharlal and Others, (2020) 8 SCC 129
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The High Court has observed that if one of the contd..
- 3 - two ingredients of Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act is not met, there shall be deemed lapse of acquisition.
However, the same is contrary to the view taken by this Court in the case of Indore Development Authority (supra).

As per the law laid down by this Court in the case of Indore Development Authority (supra), for deemed lapse under Section 24(2) of the `2013 Act, if one of two ingredients of Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act is satisfied, namely, possession taken or compensation paid, there shall not be any deemed lapse of acquisition.

Therefore, the aforesaid aspect is now required to be considered by the High Court in light of the law laid down by this Court in the case of Indore Development Authority (supra) and for that purpose the matter is required to be remitted back to the High Court.

In view of the above and for the reasons stated hereinabove,
both the appeals succeed.
The impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court is hereby quashed and set aside.

The matter is remitted to the High Court to decide and dispose of the writ petition afresh in accordance with law and on its own merits and in light of the law laid down by this Court in the case of Indore Development Authority (supra), more particularly paragraph 366 of the said decision.

The aforesaid exercise shall be completed by the contd..
- 4 - High Court within a period of nine months from the date of receipt of present order.
The present Appeals are allowed in terms of the above.
No costs.
J. [M.R. SHAH] ..J. [C.T. RAVIKUMAR]
